elements: Central carbon atom (gray sphere) fixed at the world origin
Three hydrogen atoms (small light-gray spheres) bonded to the central carbon, forming the umbrella that inverts (one of them pointing straight down so the wedge/hash flip is visible)
Three C-H bond cylinders
Leaving group X (deep red-brown sphere) on the +X side of carbon, with a C-X bond cylinder that lengthens and becomes a dotted partial bond at the transition state
Nucleophile Nu (deep red-brown sphere) on the -X side of carbon, initially a free isolated sphere, approaching along the backside 180 degrees from X
Forming Nu...C partial bond drawn as a dotted row of small spheres at the transition state
Electrostatic potential isosurface enveloping the nucleophile alone at the reactant stage: an isolated, strongly saturated deep-red sphere
Two-lobed electrostatic potential surface over the alkyl halide: saturated red over the halide lobe, blue/green over the methyl lobe
Wide symmetric three-lobed electrostatic potential surface at the transition state: red at both ends, green and yellow across the middle
Two-lobed electrostatic potential surface over the Nu-C product plus a separate saturated red halide sphere
Large bold in-scene geometry caption sprite reading 'Tetrahedral' / 'Planar' / 'Tetrahedral' under the molecule, matching the stage
In-scene magenta atom tags 'Nu', 'C', 'X' pinned in front of the translucent surface at each atom, with magenta δ⁻ tags on Nu and X at the transition state
In-scene 2D reaction-scheme panel (canvas-textured plane) standing to the right of the molecule: three stacked rows separated by downward arrows
Scheme row 1: magenta 'Nu:⁻', a plus sign, and a tetrahedral carbon with one bold wedge, one hashed bond and two plain bonds joined to a magenta X
Scheme row 2: the transition state inside black square brackets, Nu at left and X at right each with a magenta δ⁻, each tied to the carbon by a dotted line, the other three bonds coplanar
Scheme row 3: 'Nu-C' with wedge and hash reversed relative to row 1, a plus sign, and magenta 'X:⁻'
Two downward reaction arrows between the scheme rows; the row matching the current reaction coordinate is highlighted and the others dimmed
Electrostatic potential color-key strip (red most negative → orange → yellow → green → blue least negative) as a small in-scene sprite in a lower corner

interactions.label: Reaction coordinate (reactants → transition state → products)
interactions.teaches: SN2 is one continuous concerted step: the C-Nu bond forms exactly as the C-X bond breaks, the carbon flattens to planar at the halfway point and then inverts, while the red (most negative) region migrates from the free nucleophile, spreads over both ends of the planar species, and finally settles on the departing halide.
interactions.schemeLink: The in-scene scheme panel highlights row 1 for t<0.25, row 2 for 0.25<=t<=0.75, row 3 for t>0.75.

interactions.label: Layout
interactions.teaches: Seeing reactant, planar transition state and inverted product stacked in one view — exactly the source's three-row column — makes the tetrahedral → planar → tetrahedral geometry change and the red charge handoff readable at a glance instead of from memory.
interactions.layoutSpec: In 'Compare all three stages' the three frozen molecules (t=0, 0.5, 1.0) are stacked along -Y at y = +3.2, 0, -3.2, each with its own caption sprite and its own scheme row to the right; camera pulls back and the slider is disabled.

interactions.label: Display
interactions.teaches: That the colored blob and the bonded skeleton are the same molecule: the saturated red lobe always sits on whichever atom currently carries the negative charge, and the blue/green region marks the electron-poor carbon end that the nucleophile attacks.
That the three remaining substituents truly lie in one plane perpendicular to the Nu-C-X axis at the transition state, and that Nu attacks at 180 degrees from X, never from the same side.

demo_steps.title: Reactants — tetrahedral, charge on Nu
demo_steps.narration: The nucleophile is a separate, deeply saturated red sphere holding all of the negative charge. The alkyl halide is a two-lobed tetrahedral surface: red only at the halide end, blue-green over the electron-poor carbon end. The scheme panel highlights the top row, Nu:⁻ + C-X.

demo_steps.title: Backside approach
demo_steps.narration: Nu moves in along the line directly opposite the C-X bond. The C-X bond stretches, the three hydrogens start to bend away from the incoming nucleophile, and red begins to bleed from Nu toward the halide.

demo_steps.title: Planar transition state
demo_steps.narration: At the halfway point the carbon is trigonal planar with Nu and X both half-bonded at 180 degrees. The map is a wide symmetric three-lobed surface, red at both ends and green-yellow across the middle: the charge is delocalized, each of Nu and X carrying δ⁻, matching the bracketed middle row of the scheme.

demo_steps.title: Watch the umbrella flip
demo_steps.narration: With the map hidden, the skeleton alone shows the hydrogens snapping through to the far side as the new Nu-C bond shortens and the C-X bond breaks — the carbon's configuration turns inside out.

demo_steps.title: Products — inverted, charge on X
demo_steps.narration: The product is tetrahedral again but with the wedge and hash reversed, and the saturated red lobe now lives entirely on the free leaving group X:⁻.

demo_steps.title: All three stages together
demo_steps.narration: Stacked as in the textbook: tetrahedral reactants on top, the wide planar transition state in the middle, inverted tetrahedral products below. Reading down the column, the red charge leaves the nucleophile, spreads over both ends of the planar species, and settles on the halide.

plan.geometry_notes: World units ≈ Ångströms; single-stage scene spans about x ∈ [-5, +9] (molecule left, scheme panel right) and y ∈ [-3, +3]. Reaction axis is the world X axis (screen-right): Nu always on -X, X (leaving group) always on +X, central carbon fixed at the origin, molecule centered near x = -1.5 so the scheme panel can sit at its right. Bond lengths vs progress t: C-X = 1.8 (t=0) → 2.4 (t=0.5) → 4.0 (t=1); C-Nu = 4.0 (t=0) → 2.4 (t=0.5) → 1.5 (t=1), i.e. exact mirrors. C-H = 1.09 throughout. The three hydrogens lie on a cone about +X with H-C-X angle 109.5° at t=0 (umbrella opening toward Nu), exactly 90° (planar) at t=0.5, and 70.5° at t=1; hydrogens 120° apart in the YZ plane with one pointing straight down (-Y). Sphere radii: carbon 0.45, hydrogen 0.28, Nu and X 0.62, drawn dark red-brown #A0301C in ball-and-stick. Potential isosurface = metaball field with radii ~1.95 around Nu and X, ~1.45 around C, ~1.1 around each H, so t=0 reads as one isolated sphere plus a two-lobed peanut, t=0.5 as a wide symmetric three-lobed dumbbell ~7 units long, t=1 as the mirror of t=0. COLOR RAMP (must be strongly saturated at the red end, matching the source): most negative #C81E1E → #E04A20 → #F0902A → #F2DE3A → #46B45A → #2E7FD1 → least negative #1F3FA8. Point charges driving the ramp: Nu and X interpolate (-1.0, 0.0) at t=0 → (-0.5, -0.5) at t=0.5 → (0.0, -1.0) at t=1; carbon +0.25, each H +0.08. Clamp the potential range so the halide/Nu lobe hits full #C81E1E and the methyl lobe reaches green-to-blue rather than everything sitting mid-ramp. LABELS: atom tags 'Nu', 'C', 'X' in magenta #E0218A at 15–16px equivalent, and δ⁻ tags at the same size on Nu and X for 0.25<=t<=0.75; render them as depth-test-disabled sprites so they read in front of the translucent surface, each with a white rounded backing plate. Bold stage caption ('Tetrahedral' / 'Planar' / 'Tetrahedral') 18–22px, black, centered 2.2 units below the molecule. IN-SCENE SCHEME PANEL: a canvas-textured plane ~5.0 wide × 6.0 tall, centered at about (x=+6.0, y=0, z=0), facing the camera, white background with a thin gray border, occupying the right of the frame just as in the source. Its three rows top-to-bottom: (1) magenta 'Nu:⁻' + black tetrahedral carbon with one bold wedge, one hashed bond, two plain bonds, joined to magenta 'X'; (2) the same skeleton inside black square brackets, three bonds coplanar, magenta dotted lines out to 'Nu' (left) and 'X' (right), magenta 'δ⁻' above each; (3) 'Nu-C' with wedge and hash swapped relative to row 1, '+', magenta 'X:⁻'. Black downward arrows between rows. Draw the panel text at 32–40px on a 1024×1229 canvas so it resolves crisply; active row full opacity, inactive rows 35% opacity. Color key strip sprite ~2.4 × 0.35 at lower-left with end labels 'more negative' / 'less negative'. In 'Compare all three stages' the molecules sit at y = +3.2, 0, -3.2 (t = 0, 0.5, 1) each with its own caption and aligned scheme row, and the camera dollies out so all three fit at heightFraction ~0.8.
plan.notes: Build the isosurface with three.js MarchingCubes at resolution 64 (not 40) or a custom marching-cubes mesh on a 64³ grid, then run computeVertexNormals plus one round of Laplacian smoothing so no faceted quilt remains; rebuild only when the slider value changes (throttle to ~30 Hz) to stay responsive. Color per vertex by evaluating the Coulomb sum from the point charges above and mapping through the saturated ramp, with a fixed min/max clamp (not per-frame auto-range) so colors stay comparable across the reaction coordinate. Surface material: MeshPhysicalMaterial, vertexColors true, transparent, opacity 0.6, roughness 0.3, clearcoat 0.4, depthWrite false so the ball-and-stick reads through. Bonds are CylinderGeometry oriented by quaternion; partial bonds at the transition state are a row of ~7 small spheres with opacity tracking bond order. Atom tags and captions: CSS2DObject or SpriteMaterial with depthTest false and renderOrder high so they never sink behind the surface; size sprites in world units chosen so the on-screen text matches the 15–22px targets at the default camera distance. The scheme panel is real in-scene geometry (PlaneGeometry + CanvasTexture, redrawn when the active row changes) rather than an HTML overlay, so it orbits with the scene and preserves the source's left-molecules / right-scheme composition; optionally billboard it slightly toward the camera. Lighting: two directional lights plus a soft hemisphere light for smooth blob shading; keep the background white.

authoredPrompt: This figure pairs a three-step reaction scheme with electrostatic potential maps to follow an SN2 substitution, arranged in three stacked rows with the maps on the left and the structures on the right. The top row writes Nu:- in magenta, a plus sign, and a tetrahedral carbon drawn with one bold wedge, one hashed bond, and two plain bonds, joined to a magenta X; alongside it the maps show the free nucleophile as an isolated deep red sphere and the alkyl halide as a two-lobed surface labeled "Tetrahedral" whose halide end is also red. A downward arrow leads to the middle row, where the transition state sits inside square brackets with Nu at the left and X at the right, each carrying a magenta delta- and each tied to the central carbon by a dotted line while the remaining three bonds to that carbon lie in a plane; its map is a wide, symmetric three-lobed surface labeled "Planar", red at both ends and green and yellow across the middle. A second arrow reaches the product row, Nu-C with the wedge and hash now reversed, plus X:-, mapped as a lobed Nu-bearing surface labeled "Tetrahedral" beside a separate red halide sphere. Read down the column, the color scale tracks negative charge leaving the nucleophile, spreading over both ends of the planar species, and settling on the departing halide. The layout supports a single-step mechanism in which backside attack 180 degrees from the leaving group turns the carbon's substituents inside out.
authoredInteractions: - Slider for reaction progress: drag from reactants through the bracketed transition state to products, and the geometry morphs from tetrahedral to planar and back while the red electrostatic potential shifts from nucleophile to both ends to leaving group, making charge delocalization during one-step SN2 substitution clear.
authoredContext:
As shown in the figure, the SN2 reaction occurs when an electron pair on the nucleophile Nu:– forces out the group X:–, which takes with it the electron pair from the former C–X bond. This occurs through a transition state in which the new Nu–C bond is partially formed at the same time that the old C–X bond is partially broken and in which the negative charge is shared by both the incoming nucleophile and the outgoing halide ion. The transition state for this inversion has the remaining three bonds to carbon in a planar arrangement (the figure).

The transition state of an SN2 reaction has a planar arrangement of the carbon atom and the remaining three groups. Electrostatic potential maps show that negative charge is delocalized in the transition state.

The figure shows the S N 2 reaction along with their ball-and-stick model in electrostatic potential maps. Tertiary alkyl halide and substituted compound are tetrahedral, while transition state is planar.

The mechanism proposed by Hughes and Ingold is fully consistent with experimental results, explaining both stereochemical and kinetic data. Thus, the requirement for a backside approach of the entering nucleophile (180° away from the departing X group) causes the stereochemistry of the substrate to invert, much like an umbrella turning inside-out in the wind. The Hughes–Ingold mechanism also explains why second-order kinetics are observed: the SN2 reaction occurs in a single step that involves both alkyl halide and nucleophile. Two molecules are involved in the step whose rate is measured.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Work in Angstrom-like world units, 1 unit = 1 Å; whole scene spans about ±5 units along X. Reaction axis is the world X axis, screen-right: Nu always on -X, X (leaving group) always on +X, central carbon fixed at the origin. Bond lengths as a function of progress t in [0,1]: C-X = 1.8 + 1.2*t*t*... use C-X = 1.8 at t=0, 2.4 at t=0.5, 4.0 at t=1; C-Nu = 4.0 at t=0, 2.4 at t=0.5, 1.5 at t=1 (symmetric mirror). C-H = 1.09 throughout. The three hydrogens sit on a cone about the X axis: H-C-X angle = 109.5 deg at t=0 (hydrogens tilted toward -X, umbrella opening toward Nu), 90 deg (exactly planar, perpendicular to the axis) at t=0.5, and 70.5 deg at t=1 (tilted toward +X) — this single angle sweep produces the whole inversion. Hydrogens are spaced 120 deg apart in the YZ plane; keep one hydrogen pointing straight down (-Y) so the wedge/hash reversal is visible from the default camera. Sphere radii: carbon 0.45, hydrogen 0.28, halide X and nucleophile Nu 0.62 (drawn as dark red-brown #A0301C in ball-and-stick). Electrostatic potential surface = a smooth blobby isosurface (metaballs / union of scaled spheres, radius ~1.9 around Nu and X, ~1.4 around C, ~1.1 around each H) so at t=0 it reads as one isolated sphere plus a two-lobed peanut, at t=0.5 as a wide symmetric three-lobed dumbbell about 7 units long, at t=1 as a two-lobed peanut plus an isolated sphere. Potential color ramp painted on that surface: most negative red #E8746B / #D9534F, orange #E8945A, yellow #E8E06A, green #8FD18F, blue #7F9FE0 for least negative. Charge weighting: at t=0 the Nu blob is fully red and the halide lobe red while the methyl lobe of the alkyl halide is blue/green; at t=0.5 both end lobes red and the central methyl band green-to-yellow; at t=1 mirror of t=0. Geometry caption text sits centered below the 3D scene: 'Tetrahedral' for t<0.25, 'Planar' near t=0.5, 'Tetrahedral' for t>0.75. The 2D reaction-scheme panel occupies the right third of the frame, three rows stacked top to bottom with downward arrows between them, and the row matching the current slider value is highlighted while the others dim: row 1 'Nu:⁻ + C-X' with Nu, the colon-minus and X in magenta #E0218A and the carbon skeleton in black; row 2 the same skeleton inside black square brackets with magenta dotted bonds out to Nu and X and magenta δ⁻ labels above each; row 3 'Nu-C ... + X:⁻' with wedge and hash swapped relative to row 1. Black text, white background.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the electrostatic surface as a marching-cubes metaball field (three.js MarchingCubes or a custom implicit mesh) rebuilt each slider frame — resolution ~40³ is enough and keeps the drag responsive; color it per-vertex by evaluating a simple Coulomb-like potential from point charges placed on Nu, C, H and X, with the Nu/X charges linearly interpolated from (-1, 0) at t=0 through (-0.5, -0.5) at t=0.5 to (0, -1) at t=1, then mapped through the red→blue ramp. Render the surface with MeshPhysicalMaterial, transparent, opacity ~0.55, roughness 0.35, slight transmission for the glossy translucent look of the source, and depthWrite false so the ball-and-stick model reads through it. Ball-and-stick uses SphereGeometry plus CylinderGeometry bonds oriented with quaternion lookAt; partial bonds at the transition state are drawn as a row of small spheres (dotted) rather than a solid cylinder, fading the cylinder opacity in/out with bond order. Use two directional lights plus a soft hemisphere light to match the smooth shaded blobs. The 2D scheme panel is best done as an HTML/SVG overlay pinned to the right of the canvas rather than in-scene geometry, with CSS opacity for the active-row highlight. Labels 'Tetrahedral'/'Planar' as a CSS2DObject or plain HTML caption under the canvas. The play animation simply sweeps reactionProgress 0→1→0 with an ease-in-out and writes back to the slider so the two controls stay in sync.

discrepancies: Labels are effectively illegible: the only visible caption ("Tetrahedral") renders at a few pixels tall, and the Nu:⁻, C and X atom tags that the code creates are not discernible in the rendered view — the source's bold black "Tetrahedral/Planar" captions and magenta Nu/X annotations are lost.

The electrostatic-potential surface colors are muted and muddy (olive/brown/dark-red) compared with the source's vivid rainbow map (saturated red lobes, green/yellow midsection, blue patches); the blue end of the ramp never appears on the default reactant frame.
The isosurface is visibly faceted/lumpy with a quilted wireframe-like shading, whereas the source shows a smooth, glossy, softly-shaded van der Waals-style surface.

The source shows the three stages (tetrahedral reactant / planar TS / inverted tetrahedral product) simultaneously stacked for direct comparison; the generated figure only ever shows one stage at a time via the slider, so the side-by-side inversion comparison that is the point of the figure is not visible at a glance.

The 2D reaction scheme has been moved out of the figure canvas into the HTML side panel, so the 3D scene occupies only a small fraction of the viewport and the left/right composition of the source is not reproduced.
In the source the nucleophile sphere and the alkyl-halide map are drawn at comparable large scale filling the frame; here the molecule is rendered small in the corner of a mostly-empty canvas.
evaluation.notes: Chemically correct and richly interactive SN2 animation (slider, display modes, play, guided steps, clickable scheme) with the right primitives and geometry, but the ESP surface is dull and faceted rather than the source's smooth rainbow map, the molecule is rendered small, and the Nu/C/X and stage captions are far too small to read.
action_items: Increase label font sizes substantially (e.g. 18–22px for the bold stage caption, 15–16px for Nu:⁻/C/X) and verify the atom tags actually appear in front of the translucent surface so the magenta Nu/X annotations are readable.

Retune the potential ramp and field so the reactant map shows a strongly saturated red halide lobe and blue/green regions like the source, and raise the marching grid resolution (or add smoothing) to eliminate the faceted quilt-like surface.
Frame the camera so the molecule fills the canvas (larger heightFraction) and consider a near front-on view matching the source's orientation.
Optionally add a 'compare all three stages' toggle that shows reactant, planar TS and inverted product stacked simultaneously, mirroring the source layout.
plan_action_items: Plan the reaction scheme as an in-scene panel (sprite/canvas plane) beside the molecule rather than only in the side UI, so the figure's left-molecules/right-scheme composition is preserved.

demo_steps.title: Reactants — tetrahedral, charge on Nu
demo_steps.narration: The nucleophile is a separate, deeply saturated red sphere holding all of the negative charge. The alkyl halide is a two-lobed tetrahedral surface: red only at the halide end, blue-green over the electron-poor carbon end. The scheme panel highlights the top row, Nu:⁻ + C-X.

demo_steps.title: Backside approach
demo_steps.narration: Nu moves in along the line directly opposite the C-X bond. The C-X bond stretches, the three hydrogens start to bend away from the incoming nucleophile, and red begins to bleed from Nu toward the halide.

demo_steps.title: Planar transition state
demo_steps.narration: At the halfway point the carbon is trigonal planar with Nu and X both half-bonded at 180 degrees. The map is a wide symmetric three-lobed surface, red at both ends and green-yellow across the middle: the charge is delocalized, each of Nu and X carrying δ⁻, matching the bracketed middle row of the scheme.

demo_steps.title: Watch the umbrella flip
demo_steps.narration: With the map hidden, the skeleton alone shows the hydrogens snapping through to the far side as the new Nu-C bond shortens and the C-X bond breaks — the carbon's configuration turns inside out.

demo_steps.title: Products — inverted, charge on X
demo_steps.narration: The product is tetrahedral again but with the wedge and hash reversed, and the saturated red lobe now lives entirely on the free leaving group X:⁻.

demo_steps.title: All three stages together
demo_steps.narration: Stacked as in the textbook: tetrahedral reactants on top, the wide planar transition state in the middle, inverted tetrahedral products below. Reading down the column, the red charge leaves the nucleophile, spreads over both ends of the planar species, and settles on the halide.

plan.geometry_notes: World units ≈ Ångströms; single-stage scene spans about x ∈ [-5, +9] (molecule left, scheme panel right) and y ∈ [-3, +3]. Reaction axis is the world X axis (screen-right): Nu always on -X, X (leaving group) always on +X, central carbon fixed at the origin, molecule centered near x = -1.5 so the scheme panel can sit at its right. Bond lengths vs progress t: C-X = 1.8 (t=0) → 2.4 (t=0.5) → 4.0 (t=1); C-Nu = 4.0 (t=0) → 2.4 (t=0.5) → 1.5 (t=1), i.e. exact mirrors. C-H = 1.09 throughout. The three hydrogens lie on a cone about +X with H-C-X angle 109.5° at t=0 (umbrella opening toward Nu), exactly 90° (planar) at t=0.5, and 70.5° at t=1; hydrogens 120° apart in the YZ plane with one pointing straight down (-Y). Sphere radii: carbon 0.45, hydrogen 0.28, Nu and X 0.62, drawn dark red-brown #A0301C in ball-and-stick. Potential isosurface = metaball field with radii ~1.95 around Nu and X, ~1.45 around C, ~1.1 around each H, so t=0 reads as one isolated sphere plus a two-lobed peanut, t=0.5 as a wide symmetric three-lobed dumbbell ~7 units long, t=1 as the mirror of t=0. COLOR RAMP (must be strongly saturated at the red end, matching the source): most negative #C81E1E → #E04A20 → #F0902A → #F2DE3A → #46B45A → #2E7FD1 → least negative #1F3FA8. Point charges driving the ramp: Nu and X interpolate (-1.0, 0.0) at t=0 → (-0.5, -0.5) at t=0.5 → (0.0, -1.0) at t=1; carbon +0.25, each H +0.08. Clamp the potential range so the halide/Nu lobe hits full #C81E1E and the methyl lobe reaches green-to-blue rather than everything sitting mid-ramp. LABELS: atom tags 'Nu', 'C', 'X' in magenta #E0218A at 15–16px equivalent, and δ⁻ tags at the same size on Nu and X for 0.25<=t<=0.75; render them as depth-test-disabled sprites so they read in front of the translucent surface, each with a white rounded backing plate. Bold stage caption ('Tetrahedral' / 'Planar' / 'Tetrahedral') 18–22px, black, centered 2.2 units below the molecule. IN-SCENE SCHEME PANEL: a canvas-textured plane ~5.0 wide × 6.0 tall, centered at about (x=+6.0, y=0, z=0), facing the camera, white background with a thin gray border, occupying the right of the frame just as in the source. Its three rows top-to-bottom: (1) magenta 'Nu:⁻' + black tetrahedral carbon with one bold wedge, one hashed bond, two plain bonds, joined to magenta 'X'; (2) the same skeleton inside black square brackets, three bonds coplanar, magenta dotted lines out to 'Nu' (left) and 'X' (right), magenta 'δ⁻' above each; (3) 'Nu-C' with wedge and hash swapped relative to row 1, '+', magenta 'X:⁻'. Black downward arrows between rows. Draw the panel text at 32–40px on a 1024×1229 canvas so it resolves crisply; active row full opacity, inactive rows 35% opacity. Color key strip sprite ~2.4 × 0.35 at lower-left with end labels 'more negative' / 'less negative'. In 'Compare all three stages' the molecules sit at y = +3.2, 0, -3.2 (t = 0, 0.5, 1) each with its own caption and aligned scheme row, and the camera dollies out so all three fit at heightFraction ~0.8.
plan.notes: Build the isosurface with three.js MarchingCubes at resolution 64 (not 40) or a custom marching-cubes mesh on a 64³ grid, then run computeVertexNormals plus one round of Laplacian smoothing so no faceted quilt remains; rebuild only when the slider value changes (throttle to ~30 Hz) to stay responsive. Color per vertex by evaluating the Coulomb sum from the point charges above and mapping through the saturated ramp, with a fixed min/max clamp (not per-frame auto-range) so colors stay comparable across the reaction coordinate. Surface material: MeshPhysicalMaterial, vertexColors true, transparent, opacity 0.6, roughness 0.3, clearcoat 0.4, depthWrite false so the ball-and-stick reads through. Bonds are CylinderGeometry oriented by quaternion; partial bonds at the transition state are a row of ~7 small spheres with opacity tracking bond order. Atom tags and captions: CSS2DObject or SpriteMaterial with depthTest false and renderOrder high so they never sink behind the surface; size sprites in world units chosen so the on-screen text matches the 15–22px targets at the default camera distance. The scheme panel is real in-scene geometry (PlaneGeometry + CanvasTexture, redrawn when the active row changes) rather than an HTML overlay, so it orbits with the scene and preserves the source's left-molecules / right-scheme composition; optionally billboard it slightly toward the camera. Lighting: two directional lights plus a soft hemisphere light for smooth blob shading; keep the background white.

discrepancies: Color scheme of the ESP surfaces differs: the source surfaces are predominantly salmon/red with localized green-blue banding near the hydrogens, whereas the generated alkyl-halide surface is dominated by teal/green with a yellow-olive halide lobe — the halide end reads as electron-poor instead of red/electron-rich.

Atom-level labels (Nu:⁻, X, C) render very small and sit well above the spheres rather than adjacent to them; the 'Tetrahedral' caption is also much less prominent than the bold caption in the source.

The source shows all three stages stacked simultaneously plus the reaction scheme in one composition; the default view shows only the reactant row (the 'Compare all three stages' toggle does exist, so this is a default-state rather than missing-content issue).
The reaction scheme is rendered as flat SVG inside the side panel rather than as part of the figure canvas, so the side-by-side 'map + mechanism' layout of the source is not reproduced at a glance.
In the ball-and-stick model the C–X and C–H bonds are noticeably thicker/heavier than the thin stick bonds in the source, and only two of the three hydrogens read clearly at the default camera angle.
evaluation.notes: A genuinely 3D, well-built metaball electrostatic-potential surface with excellent, concept-relevant interactivity (reaction-coordinate slider, display modes, compare-stages, guided steps, clickable scheme), but the surface colouring skews too green/teal versus the source's red-dominant maps and the atom/caption labels are too small and loosely attached.

Increase label font sizes (caption ~24px bold, atom tags ~18px) and place Nu/X/C labels immediately adjacent to their spheres rather than 2+ units above them.
Thin the C–H and C–X bond cylinders to match the delicate stick bonds in the source, and tilt the default camera slightly so all three hydrogens are distinguishable.
Consider defaulting to (or auto-previewing) the 'Compare all three stages' layout so the figure first reads as the same three-row composition as the source.

The 2D reaction scheme (Nu:⁻ + C–X → [Nu···C···X]‡ → Nu–C + X:⁻) that forms the right half of the source figure is drawn only as SVG inside the control panel rather than alongside the 3D rows, so the side-by-side figure composition of the original is not reproduced in the viewport.

In row 3 the departing X sphere is fused/touching the molecular surface, whereas in the source the free halide is a clearly separated sphere well apart from the product map; row 1's Nu sphere separation is better but still closer than the source.

Ball-and-stick carbon/hydrogen atoms inside the maps are barely discernible (dark olive on olive) compared with the source where the grey C and pale H spheres and thin sticks are clearly visible through the translucent surface.
claude-opus-5-cc.notes: Composition and 3D structure of the three-stage SN2 figure are well reproduced with genuine volumetric ESP surfaces and a rich, correct set of interactions (mode toggles, reaction-coordinate slider, play, guided steps, clickable scheme), but the potential-map colouring collapses to red/olive with no rainbow gradient and the captions/atom tags are too small to read.
action_items: Rebalance the potential function and ramp so the surfaces read as salmon-red over the halide/nucleophile lobes with a genuine yellow→green→blue gradient over the C–H region, matching the printed electrostatic potential maps.
Increase caption font size (and give Nu/X tags a readable size or drop them in compare view) so 'Tetrahedral'/'Planar'/'Tetrahedral' stand out as the primary labels do in the source.

Increase the Nu···molecule and molecule···X separations in rows 1 and 3 so the free ion is a clearly detached sphere, and brighten the interior C/H spheres and sticks so they show through the translucent map.
Consider rendering the reaction scheme as a 2D overlay/panel adjacent to the 3D rows (or a toggleable side column) so the default view mirrors the two-column layout of the source figure.
